name: Lena's note
examine: Weighted down with the key bowl so it would be the first thing you saw. Her handwriting gets smaller toward the bottom of the page.
design_note: Opens the game and teaches the sorting philosophy before the player has sorted anything.

name: Mr. Rako's note
examine: Pushed through the mail slot, face down on the mat. You already know what it says. You read it anyway.
design_note: Sets the clock. The new tenants come on the 1st.

name: Key bowl
examine: Chipped ceramic, made by Mira. You've dropped keys in it a hundred times without looking at it. You look at it.

name: Muddy football boots
examine: By the door, where he kicked them off. The mud dried a long time ago.

second_look.text: The mud is from a Wednesday in March. He played four days before. Everyone said he was man of the match, and nobody can bear that it's true.

name: Bib #1
examine: Number one. Nylon, stretched at the neck from six years of being pulled on over a coat.

name: Corkboard
examine: Takeaway menus, a five-a-side schedule, a 5:45 a.m. gym class circled in pen.

second_look.text: The 5:45 class, circled. You never once knew him to be up before nine. Now you wonder which side of sleep this was on.

name: Your bag
examine: You brought it in and put it down without thinking, the way you have every month for eight months.
design_note: Locked until act 3. Contains the rent receipts.

name: The three boxes
examine: SHIP TO LENA. DONATE. LET GO. You wrote the labels yourself, in marker, standing up.
design_note: Section 4.1. No scoring, no wrong answers. The Lena box is sealed in the ending.

name: Vinyl shelf
examine: Alphabetized, rigorously, by a man who alphabetized nothing else in his life. One record is out of place.

second_look.text: The record out of place is not out of place. There is a paper sleeve behind it, filed where nobody tidying up would ever look.

design_note: Reveals demo_cdr. Gated on bass_case rather than demo_cdr: the bible's gating was circular. See docs/CONTENT_RULES.md. The player may re-shelve the record afterward, with no prompt for it.

name: Record player
examine: Lid up. Still plugged in. The needle is sitting where he left it.

second_look.text: You lift the needle off. The room goes back to the rain, and it takes a second to notice how much smaller it got.

design_note: Functional, and not sortable, which is a deliberate departure from section 4.1: examining it is what puts the demo on and takes it off again, and a sortable object stops offering Examine the moment it has been examined once. See docs/CONTENT_RULES.md. It is plugged in and it is the only thing in the flat that makes a sound he made.

name: Zlatan (monstera)
examine: Freshly repotted. The soil is still dark.

second_look.text: Repotted within his last month. He was taking care of things. You fill a glass and water it.

name: Framed hike photo (year one)
examine: Year one. The only one he ever framed. Both of you soaked through and grinning about it.

name: Shoebox of hike photos (years 2-7)
examine: Six more, loose in a shoebox, in order. He wrote on the back of every one of them.

name: Two concert tickets
examine: Two of them, paper, for a show in April. He bought them in February.

second_look.text: Two tickets. You assumed Mira, but the date is after they ended. You will never get to ask who the second one was for.

name: Library books
examine: Three of them, due back in April. One has a receipt shoved in two-thirds through, holding his place.

name: New sketchbook
examine: Barely used. Three pages, each dated in the corner, all of them inside his last month.

second_look.text: Starting again. Or trying to. Both are true.

name: Second controller
examine: The second one. Yours, functionally, for about nine years. The left stick still drifts.

name: The desk
examine: His desk. Paper everywhere. Later.
design_note: The act 1 and 2 examine text is a deferral. The scene at section 8.3 activates only after the thread is read. Hard Rule 3: the absence is the scene, and it must never be fixed.

name: Cover letter draft
examine: A printout near the top of the desk pile, marked up in red pen. He was arguing with himself and losing generously.

name: Invoice folder
examine: Polite reminders at the front, final notices at the back, in order. On the back of a gig flyer, a budget in his handwriting that almost balances.
design_note: Lives on the wardrobe top shelf but is sorted at the desk. No totals are ever shown: the shape of it is enough. Hard Rule 4, money is a thread and never the reason.

name: Low Orbit demo CD-R
examine: A paper sleeve, one line of Sharpie across it: we'll fix the mix later.
design_note: Placed in the living room rather than the bedroom, where the bible indexed it, because it is revealed behind a record on the vinyl shelf. See docs/CONTENT_RULES.md. Playing it on the old stereo gives one song, unmixed, drums too loud, alive.

name: Sofa blanket
examine: It still smells like the flat. The flat still smells like him.

name: Fridge magnets and photos
examine: Other people's weddings, a postcard from his mother, a magnet from a town neither of you has been to. Something glossy is peeking out from behind the team photo.
design_note: The corner of the photo-booth strip foreshadows Mira, well before the under-bed box opens.

name: The team photo
examine: Eleven of them squinting into the sun, one caught mid-blink. He is the only one in gloves, and the only one who looks certain about anything.
design_note: Promoted to its own object: the bible mentions it by id inside fridge_photos and uses it as the boots_muddy second-look gate.

name: Towel under the fridge
examine: Folded into quarters and wedged under the front left corner. Engineering, of a kind.

second_look.text: It works. It always worked. You just never noticed the quiet.

design_note: After the fragment, the fridge-hum audio bed drops to a muffled version. He wins, posthumously. The second look is self-gated: any examine after the first one.

name: Junk drawer
examine: Stuck. Everything in it is a monument to 'later.'

second_look.text: It gives on the third pull, the way it always did. Batteries, takeaway chopsticks, forty pen caps, and his charger, coiled the way he coiled things.

design_note: Jammed until act 2. Then it gives up batteries, takeaway chopsticks, forty pen caps, and the phone charger.

name: The chipped mug
examine: Yours, by a designation he took more seriously than most legal documents. The chip is on the left, where you drink from.

name: The blue mug
examine: Second shelf, front left, handle turned out. You have never once seen him drink from it.

second_look.text: Hers. He kept it where it had always gone, like the cupboard hadn't heard yet.

name: Vera's recipe card
examine: Grease-spotted, in his mother's handwriting, propped against the tin where he could see it while he cooked. There is a letter folded behind it.

name: Wall calendar
examine: Still on March. You could turn it. You don't.

name: Plant cuttings jar
examine: On the windowsill, roots visible through the glass. Still alive. He was propagating. Plural. Plans, plural.

name: Almost-empty cologne
examine: A centimetre left in the bottom of it. You take the cap off without deciding to.

name: The spare towel
examine: Yours. For the nights that ended here. It's been folded on this shelf for eight months.

name: Old appointment card
examine: A counselling service, three years old. CANCELLED written across it in his hand. He kept it anyway.
design_note: No commentary text anywhere near this object. The object is the text. Hard Rule 6: this and the referral letter are the only mental-health objects in the flat, and neither is medication.

name: Toothbrush cup
examine: One toothbrush. The single most ordinary object in the world, and you have to hold the sink for a second.

name: His phone
examine: Face-down on the bedside table, where they put it back. Dead. The charger wasn't with it.

second_look.text: You plug it in behind the table, where the socket has always been. Nothing happens for a while, the way nothing happens for a while.

design_note: The act 1 discovery that creates the game's engine. Read in act 3, after it has charged in real time. Section 4.5.

name: The referral letter
examine: In the bedside drawer, on top. The envelope is soft and grey along the folds, the way paper gets when it is opened and put away and opened again.
design_note: The worn envelope IS the writing. The interaction offers no judgment of any kind. Ambiguity 5: why he never called is never answered, and neither is what would have happened if he had.

name: The 4 a.m. notebook
examine: A cheap notebook on the bedside table, three entries in and blank after that. He wrote the times but never the dates.

name: The under-bed box
examine: A shoebox pushed to the far side, against the wall, where you would have to be looking to find it.
design_note: Opening it sets underbed_found and reveals the Mira thread: hoodie_mira, photobooth_strip, mira_draft, and dad_lighter.

name: The hoodie
examine: Not his size. Washed and folded before it went into the box, which is the part that gets you.

name: Photo-booth strip
examine: Four frames. They behave for the first two. By the third they are laughing, and after that neither of them looks at the camera again.

name: Mira's unsent letter
examine: Folded and refolded until the creases went soft. Never sent. Never thrown out either.
design_note: Reading it sets mira_read. Ambiguity 2: it is never dated, and whether he wrote it the week they ended or months later is not answerable.

name: His father's lighter
examine: Brass, worn smooth on one side from eight years in a pocket. It still has fuel in it.

name: Wardrobe
examine: The Low Orbit tour shirt, for a tour that never happened. A winter coat with two ticket stubs and a receipt in the pocket. A folder on the top shelf that you will get to.

name: Bass case
examine: Upright in the corner, latches still done up. Inside: the bass, and a mint tin of broken strings labeled in marker. Evidence.

name: Alarm clock
examine: Blinking 00:00 since a power cut nobody reset. Time has been optional here for a while.

name: Photo of his dad
examine: Tucked into the mirror frame, not displayed, not hidden. Kept at the exact distance he could stand.

name: Two folding chairs
examine: Two. Never one, never three. Angled slightly toward each other, the way you both left them.

name: Jar of bottle caps
examine: Years of them. An archive of good evenings, kept in glass.

name: String lights
examine: Strung corner to corner, the same way for six summers. Still, against all odds, working.
design_note: Turning them on is optional and sets lights_on. If they are on at the end, they stay on, visible from the street in the final exterior shot.

name: Stack of empty pots
examine: Terracotta, four of them, stacked and clean and waiting for spring.

second_look.text: He was getting back to it. The pots were waiting. So was everything.
